title: TDS provisions: Income-tax Act, 1961 to Income-tax Act, 2025
description: The ERP's reading, not a government table: for each provision of the Income-tax Act, 1961 under which tax was deducted at source up to 31 March 2026, and for its section 197, the provision of the Income-tax Act, 2025 that governs the same payment from 1 April 2026, or none. Section 536 of the 2025 Act repeals the 1961 Act and saves what was done under it but names no corresponding provision, and no complete official mapping was read. Each row says what ties the pair: a statement of the Income Tax Department's e-filing pages, the department's forms, or the words of the two Acts, where the Finance Act, 2025 (section 2(5), (6) and (9)) lists each 1961 section in the place where the Finance Act, 2026 (section 3(7) and (10)) lists its 2025 entry. The 1961 headings are those the department's TRACES pages show. Pairs whose 1961 side no instrument read states are left out: section 195(6), 197A and 206AA and the first proviso to section 194N.

TRACES, Income Tax Department, section codes (https://traces61contents.tdscpc.gov.in/en/section-codes-26A.html), “Last reviewed and updated on : 31-March-2026”: the heading of section 192, which the rates page does not give

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 392(1); Income-tax Act, 1961, section 192, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(9); e-filing TDS Compliance FAQs, question 20

cells.heading1961: Salary
cells.payment: any income chargeable under the head “Salaries”
cells.part: The deduction from salary; section 392(2) to (6) and (8) carry the rest of section 192's rules and are not paired one by one
cells.why: The Income Tax Department's TDS Compliance FAQs (question 20) state the pair: “TDS obligations shall be in accordance to Section 192 of the old Act”, and for salary of the tax year 2026-27, paid from April 2026 onwards, “TDS obligations shall be in accordance to Section 392(1) of the new act”. The Finance Acts agree: section 2(9) of the Finance Act, 2025 deducts tax from income chargeable under the head “Salaries” under section 192 at the rates of Part III of its First Schedule, and section 3(10)(ii) of the Finance Act, 2026 does the same for income chargeable under the head “Salaries” under section 392 other than sub-section (7).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 392(7); Income-tax Act, 1961, section 192A, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Payment of accumulated balance due to an employee.(applicable from 01.06.2015)
cells.payment: accumulated balance due to the employee participating in a recognised provident fund
cells.why: Section 392(7) deducts at 10% from the accumulated balance due to an employee participating in a recognised provident fund, under the heading of section 392, “Salary and accumulated balance due to an employee.”; section 2(6) of the Finance Act, 2025 lists section 192A among the deductions at the rates the sections specify where section 3(7) of the Finance Act, 2026 (Table, Sl. No. 2) lists 392(7).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 1(i)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194D, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(5)

cells.heading1961: Insurance Commission
cells.payment: Any income by way of remuneration or reward, whether by way of commission or otherwise, for soliciting or procuring insurance business (including business relating to the continuance, renewal or revival of insurance policies).
cells.why: Section 61 of the Finance Act, 2025 raised the limit of section 194D to twenty thousand rupees, the entry's “Threshold limit: ₹ 20,000.”; both Acts deduct it at the rates in force, section 2(5) of the Finance Act, 2025 listing section 194D where section 3(7) of the Finance Act, 2026 (Table, Sl. No. 1) lists 393(1) [Table: Sl. Nos. 1(i) and 5], and Part II of both First Schedules gives a rate “on income by way of insurance commission”.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 1(ii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194H, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Commission / Brokerage
cells.payment: Any income by way of commission [not being insurance commission referred to in serial number 1(i)] or brokerage.
cells.why: Section 63 of the Finance Act, 2025 raised the limit of section 194H to twenty thousand rupees and section 57 of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 set its rate at two per cent., the entry's “Rate: 2%” and “Threshold limit: ₹ 20,000.”; the Table of section 393(4) names the entry “Commission or Brokerage referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 1(ii)]”.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 2(i)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194-IB, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6); e-filing TDS Compliance FAQs, question 9, and FAQs for Form 141, question 2

cells.heading1961: Payment of rent by certain individuals or Hindu undivided family
cells.payment: Any income by way of rent.
cells.why: The department's forms tie the pair: its TDS Compliance FAQs (question 9) list “Form 26QC — TDS on rent by individual/HUF (Section 194 -IB)” and say “a common form i.e. Form No. 141 can be used for any of the above four type of transactions”, and its FAQs for Form 141 (question 2) name “Schedule A: TDS on rent paid by an Individual/HUF under section 393(1)”, the entry of Sl. No. 2(i). Section 59 of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 set the rate of section 194-IB at two per cent., the entry's “Rate: 2%”.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 2(ii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194-I, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Rent
cells.payment: Any income by way of rent.
cells.why: Section 64 of the Finance Act, 2025 spares under section 194-I rent credited or paid for a month or part of a month that does not exceed fifty thousand rupees, the entry's “Threshold limit [for (a) and (b)]: ₹ 50,000 for a month or part of a month.”; the entry's rates (a) and (b) answer TRACES's codes 194I(a) and 194I(b), and the Table of section 393(4) names the entry “Rent referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 2(ii)]”.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 3(i)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194-IA, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6); e-filing TDS Compliance FAQs, question 9, and FAQs for Form 141, question 2

cells.heading1961: Transfer of certain immovable property other than agriculture land (w.e.f. 1-6-2013)
cells.payment: Any consideration for transfer of any immovable property (other than agricultural land).
cells.why: The department's forms tie the pair: its TDS Compliance FAQs (question 9) list “Form 26QB — TDS on purchase of immovable property (Section 194 -IA)” and say “a common form i.e. Form No. 141 can be used for any of the above four type of transactions”, and its FAQs for Form 141 (question 2) name “Schedule B: TDS on transfer of immovable property under section 393(1)”, the entry of Sl. No. 3(i). The Table's heading of the entry, “Payment on transfer of certain immovable property other than agricultural land”, is the 1961 heading as the TRACES section codes give it, and Note 1 counts “the aggregate of the amounts paid or payable by all the transferees to the transferor or all the transferors”, as section 58 of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 made section 194-IA count it.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 3(ii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194-IC, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Payment under Specified agreement
cells.payment: Any consideration, not being consideration in kind, under the agreement referred to in section 67(14).
cells.why: The entry deducts from consideration under the agreement referred to in section 67(14), which section 67(15)(b) defines as a “specified agreement”, the word of TRACES's heading of section 194-IC; section 2(6) of the Finance Act, 2025 lists section 194-IC where section 3(7) of the Finance Act, 2026 (Table, Sl. No. 2) lists Sl. No. 3 of the Table of section 393(1).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 3(iii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194LA, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Immovable Property
cells.payment: Any sum, being in the nature of— (a) compensation or the enhanced compensation; or (b) consideration or the enhanced consideration, on account of compulsory acquisition, under any law for the time being in force, of any immovable property (other than agricultural land).
cells.why: Section 67 of the Finance Act, 2025 raised the limit of section 194LA to five lakh rupees, the entry's “Threshold limit: ₹ 5,00,000.”, and the Table of section 393(4) names the entry “Compensation on acquisition of certain immovable property referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 3(iii)]”, as the TRACES section codes name section 194LA.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 4(i)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194K, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Payment of Dividend by Mutual Funds (Applicable From 01-Apr-2020)
cells.payment: Any income in respect of— (a) units of a Mutual Fund specified under Schedule VII (Table: Sl. No. 20 or 21); or (b) units from the Administrator of the specified undertaking; or (c) units from the specified company.
cells.why: Section 66 of the Finance Act, 2025 raised the limit of section 194K to ten thousand rupees, the entry's “Threshold limit: ₹ 10,000.”, and the Table of section 393(4) names the entry “Income in respect of units referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 4(i)]”; section 2(6) of the Finance Act, 2025 lists section 194K where section 3(7) of the Finance Act, 2026 (Table, Sl. No. 2) lists Sl. No. 4 of the Table of section 393(1).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 4(ii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194LBA, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Certain income from units of a business trust to Residents
cells.payment: Any distributed income referred to in section 223, being of the nature referred to in Schedule V (Table: Sl. Nos. 3 and 4), payable to a unitholder of a Business Trust.
cells.part: Distributions to a unit holder resident in India
cells.why: The Table of section 393(4) names the entry “Income from units of a business trust referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 4(ii)]”, in the words of TRACES's heading of section 194LBA, and section 2(6) of the Finance Act, 2025 lists section 194LBA where section 3(7) of the Finance Act, 2026 (Table, Sl. No. 2) lists Sl. No. 4 of the Table of section 393(1), which deducts from payments to a resident.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 4(iii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194LBB, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Income in respect of units of investment fund.
cells.payment: Any income, other than that proportion of income which is exempt under Schedule V (Table: Sl. No. 2), in respect of units of an investment fund specified in section 224, payable to its unitholder.
cells.part: Unit holders resident in India
cells.why: The entry deducts from income in respect of units of an investment fund specified in section 224, which the Table of section 393(4) names “Income in respect of units of investment fund” for the payments to non-residents, TRACES's heading of section 194LBB; section 2(6) of the Finance Act, 2025 lists section 194LBB where section 3(7) of the Finance Act, 2026 (Table, Sl. No. 2) lists Sl. No. 4 of the Table of section 393(1).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 4(iv)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194LBC, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Income in respect of investment in securitisation trust.
cells.payment: Any income, in respect of an investment in a securitisation trust specified in section 221 to an investor.
cells.part: Investors resident in India
cells.why: Section 68 of the Finance Act, 2025 gave section 194LBC its rate in the words “at the rate of ten per cent.”, the entry's “Rate: 10%”, and section 2(6) of the Finance Act, 2025 lists section 194LBC where section 3(7) of the Finance Act, 2026 (Table, Sl. No. 2) lists Sl. No. 4 of the Table of section 393(1).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 5(i)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 193, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(5)

cells.heading1961: Interest on securities
cells.payment: Any income by way of Interest on securities.
cells.why: Section 56 of the Finance Act, 2025 limited section 193 to “the amount or the aggregate of amounts exceeding ten thousand rupees during the financial year”, the entry's “Threshold limit: ₹ 10,000.”, and the Table of section 393(4) names the entry “Interest on securities referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 5(i)]”, TRACES's heading of section 193; both Acts deduct it at the rates in force (Finance Act, 2025, section 2(5); Finance Act, 2026, section 3(7), Table, Sl. No. 1).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 5(ii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194A, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(5)

cells.heading1961: Banks / Co-operative society engaged in business of banking / Post Office
cells.payment: Any income by way of interest other than interest on securities.
cells.part: Interest paid by a banking company, a co-operative society carrying on the business of banking or a post office
cells.why: Section 58 of the Finance Act, 2025 raised the limits of section 194A(3)(i) to fifty thousand rupees and, in its third proviso, to one lakh rupees, the entry's “(a) ₹ 1,00,000 in the case of a senior citizen; (b) ₹ 50,000 in case of person other than senior citizen.”; the Table of section 393(4) names the entry “Interest other than interest on securities referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 5(ii) and 5(iii)]”, and both Acts deduct it at the rates in force (Finance Act, 2025, section 2(5); Finance Act, 2026, section 3(7), Table, Sl. No. 1).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 5(iii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194A, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(5)

cells.heading1961: Interest other than interest on securities - in any Others Case
cells.payment: Any income being interest other than interest on securities.
cells.part: Interest paid by any other payer
cells.why: Section 58 of the Finance Act, 2025 raised the limit of sub-clause (d) of section 194A(3)(i) to ten thousand rupees, the entry's “Threshold limit: ₹ 10,000.”; the entry's payer is a specified person other than the banking company, co-operative society or post office of Sl. No. 5(ii), and both Acts deduct it at the rates in force (Finance Act, 2025, section 2(5); Finance Act, 2026, section 3(7), Table, Sl. No. 1).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(i)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194C, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6); e-filing TDS Compliance FAQs, question 2, and Tax Payments FAQs, question 5

cells.heading1961: Payment to Contractors
cells.payment: Any sum for carrying out any work (including supply of labour for carrying out any work) in pursuance of a contract between the contractor and a designated person.
cells.part: Work for a designated person; work for an individual or Hindu undivided family who is not one falls under section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(ii)], with section 194M
cells.why: The department's TDS Compliance FAQs (question 2) state the pair: for payments for March 2026 credited on 31 March 2026 “TDS obligation shall be under Section 194C of old Act.”, and under the new Act “TDS obligations shall be under Section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(i)] of the new Act.”; its Tax Payments FAQs (question 5) add that “the firm must quote Section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(i)] of the new Act, and not Section 194C of the old Act.” The words agree: section 402(47) keeps out of “work” what Explanation (iv) to section 194C, as section 53 of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 substituted it, keeps out: “manufacturing or supplying a product according to the requirement or specification of a customer by using material purchased from a person, other than such customer or associate of such customer”, and the Table of section 393(4) names the entry “Payments to contractors referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(i)]”.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(ii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194M, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6); e-filing TDS Compliance FAQs, question 9, and FAQs for Form 141, question 2

cells.heading1961: Payment of certain sums by certain individuals or Hindu undivided family
cells.payment: Any sum–– (a) for carrying out any work (including supply of labour for carrying out any work) in pursuance of a contract; or (b) by way of fees for professional services; or (c) by way of commission [not being insurance commission referred to in serial number 1(i)] or brokerage.
cells.why: The department's forms tie the pair: its TDS Compliance FAQs (question 9) list “Form 26QD — TDS on payments by individuals/HUFs to contractors and professionals (Section 194M)” and say “a common form i.e. Form No. 141 can be used for any of the above four type of transactions”, and its FAQs for Form 141 (question 2) name “Schedule C: TDS on payment made by an Individual/HUF to contractors or professionals”, which it places under section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(ii)]. Section 60 of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 set the rate of section 194M at two per cent., the entry's “Rate: 2%”.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(iii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194J, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Fees for Professional/Technical Services
cells.payment: Any sum by way of–– (a) fees for professional services; or (b) fees for technical services; or (c) remuneration or fees or commission by whatever name called, other than those on which tax is deductible under section 392, to a director of a company; or (d) royalty; or (e) any sum referred to in section 26(2)(h).
cells.why: Where Explanation (iv) to section 194C, as section 53 of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 substituted it, keeps “any sum referred to in sub-section (1) of section 194J” out of “work”, section 402(47) keeps out “any sum referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(iii)]”; section 65 of the Finance Act, 2025 raised the limit of section 194J(1) to fifty thousand rupees, the entry's “Threshold limit: (i) for (a), (b), (d) and (e) of Col. B: ₹ 50,000.”, and the Table of section 393(4) names the entry “Fees for professional or technical services referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(iii)]”.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) (Table: Sl. No. 7); Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Dividends
cells.payment: Any dividend (including dividend on preference shares) declared.
cells.why: Section 57 of the Finance Act, 2025 raised the limit in clause (b) of the first proviso to section 194 to ten thousand rupees, the limit up to which the Table of section 393(4) (Sl. No. 10(f)) spares a dividend paid to an individual shareholder by any mode other than cash; the Table names the entry “Dividend referred to in section 393(1) (Table: Sl. No. 7)”, and section 2(6) of the Finance Act, 2025 lists section 194 where section 3(7) of the Finance Act, 2026 (Table, Sl. No. 2) lists Sl. No. 7 of the Table of section 393(1).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(i)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194DA, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Payment in respect of life insurance policy (applicable from 01.10.2014)
cells.payment: Any sum under a life insurance policy, including the sum allocated as bonus on such policy, other than the amount not includible in the total income under Schedule II (Table: Sl. No. 2).
cells.why: Section 54 of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 set the rate of section 194DA at two per cent., the entry's “Rate: 2% on income comprised in such sum.”, and the Table of section 393(6) names the entry “payment in respect of life insurance policy referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(i)]”, in the words of TRACES's heading of section 194DA.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(ii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194Q, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: TDS on Purchase of Goods exceeding Rs. 50 Lakhs (Applicable From 01-July-2021)
cells.payment: Any sum exceeding fifty lakh rupees for purchase of any goods.
cells.why: The entry deducts from “Any sum exceeding fifty lakh rupees for purchase of any goods.”, as TRACES heads section 194Q, and its Note 1(a) excludes “a transaction on which tax is deductible or collectible under any of the provisions of the Act”, where section 69 of the Finance Act, 2025 struck the exception for section 206C(1H) out of section 194Q(5)(b); section 2(6) of the Finance Act, 2025 lists section 194Q where section 3(7) of the Finance Act, 2026 (Table, Sl. No. 2) lists Sl. No. 8(ii) of the Table of section 393(1).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(iii)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194P, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(9)

cells.heading1961: TDS in case of Specified Senior Citizen
cells.payment: Total income of a specified senior citizen after giving effect to deduction allowable under Chapter VIII and rebate allowable under section 156.
cells.why: Section 2(9) of the Finance Act, 2025 computes the tax deducted under section 194P at the rates of Part III of its First Schedule, and section 3(10)(iii) of the Finance Act, 2026 does the same where “income-tax has to be deducted under section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(iii)] of the said Act”; the entry's payer is the specified bank of a specified senior citizen, as TRACES heads section 194P.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(iv)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194R, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: TDS in case any benefit or perquisite (arising from business or the exercise of a profession) is provided (Applicable From 01-July-2022)
cells.payment: Any benefit or perquisite, whether convertible into money or not, arising from business or the exercise of a profession of any resident.
cells.why: The entry deducts from “Any benefit or perquisite, whether convertible into money or not, arising from business or the exercise of a profession of any resident.”, which TRACES's heading of section 194R describes in the same words, and section 2(6) of the Finance Act, 2025 lists section 194R where section 3(7) of the Finance Act, 2026 (Table, Sl. No. 2) lists Sl. No. 8(iv) of the Table of section 393(1).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(v)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194-O, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: TDS on e-commerce participants (Applicable From 01-Oct-2020)
cells.payment: Any sum on account of sale of goods or provision of services by an e-commerce participant, facilitated by an e-commerce operator through its digital or electronic facility or platform.
cells.why: Section 61 of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 set the rate of section 194-O at 0.1 per cent., the entry's “Rate: 0.1% of gross amount of such sale or services or both.”, and the Table of section 393(4) names the entry “Payment by e-commerce operator to e-commerce participant referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(v)]”, which the TRACES section codes head “Payment of certain sums by e-commerce operator to e-commerce participant”.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(vi)]; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194S, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6); e-filing TDS Compliance FAQs, question 9, and FAQs for Form 141, question 2

cells.heading1961: TDS on payment on transfer of Virtual Digital Asset ( Applicable From 01-July-2022)
cells.payment: Any sum by way of consideration for transfer of a virtual digital asset.
cells.why: The department's forms tie the pair: its TDS Compliance FAQs (question 9) list “Form 26QE — TDS on transfer of virtual digital assets (Section 194S)” and say “a common form i.e. Form No. 141 can be used for any of the above four type of transactions”, and its FAQs for Form 141 (question 2) name “Schedule D: TDS on payment made by an Individual/HUF on transfer of Virtual Digital Assets (VDA)”, which it places under section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(vi)]. The Table of section 393(4) names the entry “Payment on transfer of virtual digital asset referred to in section 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(vi)]”.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(2) (Table: Sl. No. 1); Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194E, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Payment to Non-Resident Sportsmen or Sports Association
cells.payment: Any income referred to in section 211.
cells.why: The entry deducts from income referred to in section 211, headed “Tax on non-resident sportsmen or sports associations.”, and section 2(6) of the Finance Act, 2025 lists section 194E where section 3(7) of the Finance Act, 2026 (Table, Sl. No. 2) lists Sl. Nos. 1 to 6 of the Table of section 393(2).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 393(2) (Table: Sl. No. 2); Income-tax Act, 1961, section 194LC, as listed in the Finance Act, 2025, section 2(6)

cells.heading1961: Income by way of interest by an Indian specified company to a non-resident / foreign company on foreign currency approved loan /long-term infrastructure bonds from outside India (applicable from July 1, 2012)
cells.payment: Any income by way of interest payable in respect of moneys borrowed in foreign currency from a source outside India,— (a) under a loan agreement or issue of long-term infrastructure bond on or after the 1st July, 2012 but before the 1st July, 2023; or (b) by way of issue of any long-term bond on or after the 1st October, 2014 but before the 1st July, 2023, which is approved by the Central Government in this behalf.
cells.part: Interest on moneys borrowed in foreign currency under a loan agreement or by way of long-term bonds
cells.why: Part II of the First Schedule to the Finance Act, 2025 leaves out “income by way of interest referred to in section 194LB or section 194LC” where Part II of the Finance Act, 2026 leaves out “income by way of interest referred to in section 393(2) [Table: Sl. Nos. 2 to 5] of the said Act”, and section 397(2)(c)(i) of the 2025 Act spares a non-resident from the higher rate without a PAN on “payment of interest on long-term bonds as specified in section 393(2) (Table: Sl.
